scenes.title: The Anatomy of Operational Risk & Rogue Trading

beatOutlines.textOutline: A risk director defines operational risk: catastrophic financial loss from failed internal processes, rogue trading, or control breakdowns ([fact-01]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The mentor establishes non-negotiable controls: daily independent mark-to-market accounting and strict segregation of trading and settlement duties ([fact-02]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: They caution against abnormal outperformance, which almost always reflects hidden tail risk or leverage rather than foresight ([fact-03]).

scenes.title: Barings Bank vs. Société Générale Control Failures

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Barings Bank (1995): Nick Leeson combined front-office trading and back-office settlement in Singapore, hiding losses in error account 88888 ([fact-04]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Société Générale (2008): Jérôme Kerviel accumulated €50B in unauthorized futures by entering fictitious offsetting forwards using insider compliance knowledge ([fact-06]).

scenes.title: Deconstructing Gross Terminal Payoff vs. Net Trading Profit

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Gross Payoff: terminal cash flow upon contract expiration max(S - K, 0) without accounting for acquisition costs ([fact-09]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Net Trading Profit: strictly deducting initial option premium paid ($	ext{Profit} = 	ext{Payoff} - 	ext{Premium}$) to establish true economic returns ([fact-09]).

beatOutlines.textOutline: Examine Rogue Trading Scale: Barings lost £827M and Allfirst lost $691M through unauthorized directional bets and fictitious trades ([fact-05], [fact-07]).

beatOutlines.textOutline: Examine LTCM Leverage Collapse: lost $4.6B in 1998 due to 25:1 balance-sheet leverage and $1 trillion in off-balance-sheet swaps ([fact-08]).

scenes.title: Normal VaR Models vs. Extreme Tail-Risk Stress Testing

beatOutlines.textOutline: Balance Normal VaR Models: evaluate potential losses under standard market distributions but fail entirely during extreme market shocks ([fact-10]).

beatOutlines.textOutline: Balance Rigorous Stress Testing: models catastrophic historical scenarios (1987, 1998, 2008) including asset illiquidity and margin call spikes ([fact-10]).

summarySteps: 1. Operational Risk ([fact-01]): Risk of catastrophic financial loss from failed internal processes, rogue trading, or control breakdowns.
2. Segregation of Duties ([fact-02]): Mandatory separation of trading execution from back-office settlement with independent daily mark-to-market accounting.
3. Illusion of Outperformance ([fact-03]): Exceptional trading returns almost always reflect unacknowledged short option tail risk or hidden leverage.
4. Barings Bank Collapse ([fact-04], [fact-05]): Nick Leeson's dual trading/settlement role caused an £827M loss following the Kobe earthquake.
5. SocGen & Allfirst ([fact-06], [fact-07]): Jérôme Kerviel and John Rusnak bypassed controls using fictitious trades and insider compliance knowledge.
6. LTCM Failure ([fact-08]): 25:1 leverage and $1 trillion in swaps collapsed during the 1998 Russian default liquidity freeze.
7. Net Profit Invariant ([fact-09]): $	ext{Profit} = 	ext{Payoff} - 	ext{Premium}$ explicitly deducting initial option purchase costs from gross cashflows.
8. Rigorous Stress Testing ([fact-10]): Supplementing normal VaR models with catastrophic historical shock scenarios like 1987, 1998, and 2008.
bottomTakeaway: Operational risk and organizational control failures—exemplified by Barings, SocGen, and LTCM—prove that institutional survival depends entirely on independent daily valuations, strict segregation of duties, and rigorous tail-risk stress testing ([fact-02], [fact-04], [fact-08], [fact-10]).
